metadata.creator: Upham, Alfred H.
metadata.description: Alfred H. Upham, identified by his title as president, writes to Murray Sheehan at the Royal Thai Legation in Washington, D.C. He asks Sheehan to extend an invitation to a Thai minister in Washington to deliver Miami University's commencement address on 8 June 1942 and to escort him to Oxford if possible. Upham also remarks on the possible recall of the minister, international conditions in the Pacific area, and the performance of Thai students at Miami.
metadata.title: Letter to Mr. Murray Sheehan from the president, 19 November 1941
metadata.transcript:
[page 1]
November 19, 1941

Mr. Murray Sheehan
Royal Thai Legation
2300 Kalorama Road
Washington, D. C. [District of Columbia]

Dear Murray:

I have just had word from the problem of finding speakers for our Commencement exercises next June. Naturally, I am greatly attracted by your suggestion that there is a certain minister from Thai in Washington who would qualify in every way as our speaker on the regular commencement program. I have only two reservations which are quite obvious: one, that for some reason or other this man also may be recalled before our Commencement date; the other, that international friendships in the Pacific area may crack all to pieces before that time so that there may be no Thailand minister in Washington at all. However, I am willing to take chances on these contingencies. There is a third difficulty in which I know you can help me. That is, my utter inability to pronounce any of these Siamese names correctly in public.

Seriously, I should be glad to have you extend our invitation to the Minister to deliver the Commencement address to the graduates of Miami University on the morning of Monday, June 8, 1942, which is our regular Commencement date. If he can arrange to undertake this responsibility, I shall hope of course that you may find it convenient to escort him out here and enjoy with him the Commencement exercises that always characterize Miami University.

We greatly miss some of our friends from the Thailand boys who were with us last year. Those who are here at the present time, however, are giving an excellent account of themselves.

With all good wishes,

Very truly yours,

President
